Questions: How does Wyckoff identify when accumulation is beginning?

Questions: What signals indicate accumulation is in its early stages versus late stages?
Answers: Early accumulation shows erratic price action with high volume selling climaxes, while late accumulation displays narrowing price ranges, successful tests on low volume, and springs that shake out remaining weak holders before markup begins.
Label: Timing

Questions: How long does Wyckoff typically observe an accumulation pattern before considering entry?
Answers: Wyckoff observes accumulation for weeks to months, ensuring the pattern develops fully with multiple tests of support, diminishing selling pressure, and clear signs that supply has been absorbed before entering.
Label: Timing

Questions: What is a Preliminary Support (PS) and how does it affect entry timing?
Answers: Preliminary Support is the first indication that selling pressure is being absorbed after a downtrend. While it signals accumulation may be starting, Wyckoff waits for further confirmation through Selling Climax and tests before entering.
Label: Timing

Questions: What is a Selling Climax (SC) and should Wyckoff enter immediately after seeing one?
Answers: A Selling Climax is a period of intense panic selling on extremely high volume that exhausts sellers. Wyckoff does not enter immediately, as he waits for the Automatic Rally and subsequent tests to confirm accumulation is underway.
Label: Timing

Questions: What is an Automatic Rally (AR) and what does it tell Wyckoff about timing?
Answers: An Automatic Rally is the sharp rebound after a Selling Climax. It shows the extent of buyer interest, but Wyckoff waits for a Secondary Test to see if supply has truly been absorbed before timing his entry.
Label: Timing

Questions: What is a Secondary Test (ST) and why is it important for entry timing?
Answers: A Secondary Test occurs when price returns to the Selling Climax area on lower volume. Successful tests with reduced volume and narrow spreads confirm sellers are exhausted, bringing Wyckoff closer to entry timing.
Label: Timing

Questions: How many tests of support does Wyckoff prefer to see before entering?
Answers: Wyckoff prefers to see multiple tests (typically 3-5) of the support level, each on progressively lower volume with narrow price spreads, confirming that all available supply has been absorbed by institutional buyers.
Label: Timing

Questions: What does absorption of supply mean and how does it guide timing?
Answers: Absorption of supply means all available sellers at lower prices have been exhausted as institutions quietly buy. Wyckoff times entries after this absorption is confirmed through successful low-volume tests of support.
Label: Timing

Questions: How does Wyckoff distinguish between accumulation and a continuation of the downtrend?
Answers: He distinguishes by analyzing volume and price action: accumulation shows declining volume on down moves with price holding support, while downtrend continuation shows expanding volume on declines breaking through support levels.
Label: Timing

Questions: What is a test in the middle of the range and what does it signal for timing?
Answers: A test in the middle of the range on low volume indicates that even at higher prices within the accumulation zone, there's no significant supply. This strengthens the case that accumulation is maturing and entry timing is approaching.
Label: Timing

Questions: How does the width of the accumulation trading range affect Wyckoff's timing decisions?

Label: Timing

Questions: What role does the Cause play in Wyckoff's entry timing?
Answers: The Cause is the amount of accumulation (time and volume) that builds potential energy for the subsequent move. A larger Cause suggests a bigger Effect, so Wyckoff times entries after sufficient Cause has been built for worthwhile targets.
Label: Timing

Questions: How does Wyckoff time entries when accumulation occurs within a larger uptrend?

Questions: How many failed rally attempts does Wyckoff observe before exiting?

Questions: What does distribution of supply mean and how does it guide exit timing?

Questions: How does Wyckoff distinguish between distribution and a consolidation before continuation higher?

Questions: What is an Upthrust (UT) and why is it a critical exit signal?

Questions: How does the width of the distribution trading range affect Wyckoff's exit timing?

Questions: What role does the Effect play in Wyckoff's exit timing during distribution?
